identity.title: Differential Impact of CRISPR/Cas9-Mediated OsMIR396ef Mutagenesis on Yield Components Across Eight Diverse Rice Varieties.

content.abstract: Substantial gains in rice productivity are a continual demand for breeders, farmers, as well as consumers. Identifying and introducing favorable yield-related genes in elite cultivars is the most efficient strategy for increasing yield. So far, many yield-related genes in rice have been cloned. However, rice varieties with a vast diversity of genetic constitutions differ tremendously in the levels of grain yield. Here, we edited yield-related MIR396e and MIR396f genes in eight japonica rice varieties and found that mutation efficiency varied with genetic background in the T0 generation. Notably, the knockout of MIR396e and MIR396f genes resulted in increased leaf, panicle, and grain size in all eight genetic backgrounds. However, plant height, culm strength, grain number per panicle, and seed setting rate varied with different genetic backgrounds. Results also showed that among the eight varieties, grain yield increased in five different rice varieties compared to the corresponding wild type, while three of them had decreased yield due to the reduced number of grains per panicle or the seed-setting rate. Thus, our findings broaden the understanding that OsmiR396 can have diverse, even opposing effects on grain yield and plant architecture among genetically distinct rice varieties.
